nodes.text: Join the Wine Wench Wine Up

nodes.alt: Alana Kaye in turquoise with the Wine Wench seal.

children.text: Alana Kaye came to wine writing by way of theatre, food and books. The Wine Wench grew out of a wish to talk about the people who make wine and the pleasure of drinking it, in language everyone can join in with.

Based in the Southern Highlands of New South Wales, Alana champions Australian producers. A McLaren Vale grenache, Adelaide Hills pinot grigio, Margaret River rosé or Tasmanian sparkling can all find a place at her table. Rosé rarely has to wait for an invitation.
Thirsty Hungry is Alana’s food-and-wine video series for nights in. Each episode starts with a bottle and something to eat, whether that means cooking dinner or picking up a favourite local takeaway.

children.alt: Alana’s food and wine pairing series

children.text: Winemaker conversations, tasting features, photography and reels for a winery or food business. Alana especially enjoys telling the stories of small, family-run and sustainability-minded producers. Ask for the current rates card.
A content plan for your own Facebook and Instagram accounts, from the first planning conversation to photography, posting and community management.
Tasting notes for a new vintage, bottle labels, website and search copy, newsletters, customer emails, SMS campaigns, print articles and interviews.
2 Instagram posts, 2 Facebook posts and 3 stories weekly.
3 Instagram posts, 3 Facebook posts and 5 stories weekly. Monthly reels included: 1.
5 Instagram posts, 5 Facebook posts and 8 stories weekly. Monthly reels included: 2.

The published packages include community management and the option to run advertising with a separate ad budget. A one-off $399 setup covers a half-day content shoot, editing and a library the client keeps. Custom plans, influencer campaigns, newsletters and blog writing are available by enquiry. Ask Alana to confirm current pricing.

Planning a Southern Highlands stay? Alana’s at-home tasting concept brings regional wines to your accommodation. The original listing marks the service as coming soon. Send your preferred date and group details to ask about availability and pricing.
The published calendar currently lists no services. Enquire about future dates.

A restaurant scene needed a convincing exchange between a diner and a sommelier. With a menu and a screenplay to work from, Alana had to choose a wine that made sense both on the table and in the dialogue.
A gift of Luigi Bormioli glassware inspired two drinks: the Old Cuban Fizzball and a Limonberry Spritz. The second starts well before cocktail hour, with homemade limoncello.
A fish curry and a Victorian chardonnay are the starting point for this Sip & Eat dinner. Alana puts the recipe, the bottle and the music together so you can try the pairing at home.

The road from Sydney takes in Rylstone, De Beaurepaire and Baker Williams before a night at Roth’s. The weekend continues through Lowe, Cellar by Gilbert, Di Lusso, Moothi and Logan, with tasting picks along the way.
A bottle of sangiovese meets a home-cooked take on moussaka. The original kitchen notes lay out the ingredients and method, followed by a tasting and a soundtrack for dinner.

children.alt: Excuse me postman, can I have my Mal-bec please?

children.text: Excuse me postman, can I have my Mal-bec please?
April 17 puts malbec in the spotlight. This introduction follows the grape from its French names and origins to the glass, with ideas for what to eat and listen to alongside it.
A Barossa grenache puts Rosenvale’s vineyards at the centre of this tasting. Alana looks at the people behind the bottle before choosing its food, soundtrack and occasion.
Rosé, pinot and bubbles share the tasting table in this look at Tipsy Aunt Flo. Alana matches each wine to food, music and an occasion, and explores the producer’s support for menstrual equity.
At his Mudgee cellar door, winemaker David Lowe talks about the bottles that first caught his attention, what still surprises him and the wine he would take to a desert island.
After trying Riversands’ bubbles, Alana returns to the Queensland producer for a fortified wine with a particularly memorable name. Her tasting includes a suggested meal, mood and playlist pairing.
What can a bottle purchase support? Alana follows the projects behind Tipsy Aunt Flo, Little Giant, Tread Softly, The Hidden Sea and Little Ripples, from wombat welfare to clean water.
From santé and salud to kanpai and skål, a shared toast has plenty of local expressions. Alana follows the words and customs behind raising a glass.

Two sparkling wines introduce Riversands, a Queensland winery whose labels tell stories about the district. Alana opens the gifted bottles and pairs each with a dish, a song and a reason to celebrate.

children.alt: To decant, or not to decant?

children.text: To decant, or not to decant?
A decanter can do two jobs: leave sediment behind and give a wine more contact with air. This guide explains when each matters and how to choose a vessel for the bottle you have.

A cellar-door trail close to home: Artemis, Mount Ashby, Tertini, Eling Forest, Cuttaway Hill and Cherry Tree Hill. Alana shares the stops and bottles that shaped her original Southern Highlands shortlist.
Champagne, crémant, cava and prosecco all fizz, but they get there by different routes. Alana follows the traditional, transfer and tank methods from fermentation to finished bottle.
Amanda Yallop, group wine director at Fink, talks about restaurant wine lists, the pleasure of unexpected matches, the bottles open in her kitchen and where she would travel for a glass.
Cockfighter’s Ghost, Audrey Wilkinson, Miles From Nowhere, Artemis, Bird in Hand and AIX make up this spring rosé selection, spanning local favourites and a French pour.
The colour of a rosé is only one clue to what is in the glass. This early Wine Wench feature explores the style behind one of Alana’s favourite pours.
Behind the medals are blind flights, judging panels and a lot of tasting. This guide follows the show process through to trophies, with a look at the Jimmy Watson award.
Gold, silver, bronze, double gold and trophies can share the same crowded bottle label. Alana unpacks the scoring bands and what the different awards tell a shopper.
Taste the dish and the wine together. Sweetness, salt, acidity and bitterness change the way each comes across, and matching similar flavours gives a different result from choosing a contrast.
Start with the colour, give the glass a swirl, then smell before tasting. Alana breaks the sip down into acidity, sweetness, alcohol and tannin so you can put words to what you notice.
